hooks.text: A spacecraft designed to die in thirty-two minutes lasted two hours.
A lander built for thirty-two minutes survived two hours on Venus.
A Soviet probe survived the solar system's most crushing world.

title: The Soviet Lander That Defied Death on Venus
description: In 1982, the Soviet Venera 13 lander touched down on the hostile surface of Venus. Designed to survive for only 32 minutes, it shocked engineers by operating for over two hours.

beats.text: A spacecraft designed to die in thirty-two minutes lasted two hours.
On March 1, 1982, the Soviet Union's Venera 13 lander descended through the clouds of Venus.
beats.visual: artist's concept of the Venera 13 probe descending through Venus's atmosphere, 1982

beats.text: The probe touched down near Phoebe Regio, facing ninety atmospheres of pressure and temperatures around four hundred sixty degrees Celsius.
beats.visual: global radar map of Venus showing Phoebe Regio region, 1990

beats.text: Safe inside its armored hull, Venera 13 drilled into the rocky ground to analyze a soil sample.
beats.visual: diagram of the Soviet Venera lander surface drilling mechanism, 1982

beats.text: It also captured and transmitted the first color photographs ever taken from the surface of another planet.
beats.visual: first color panorama photograph of the Venusian surface from Venera 13, 1982

beats.text: Decades later, a Russian scientist claimed these photos showed moving alien life, like a scorpion.
beats.visual: cropped Venera 13 photograph showing the landing site rocks, 1982

beats.text: But experts proved the mysterious alien was actually just the lander's discarded camera lens cap.
beats.visual: Venera 13 surface photograph highlighting the discarded camera lens cap, 1982

beats.text: In 1982, Soviet engineers celebrated as this historic machine defied its death sentence on Venus.
beats.visual: Soviet engineers inspecting a Venera spacecraft model in a cleanroom, 1981

better_than_last: Implemented a more engaging debunk-style twist before the loop to drive audience curiosity and retention, building on lessons from ep028.
